key_insight: A convex optimization method projects an initial matrix onto the elliptope to generate valid correlation matrices that match a graph’s sparsity pattern and can be tuned to control the mean off-diagonal correlation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a controllable way to synthesize realistic correlation matrices for benchmarking graphical model inference, especially in neuroscience and finance where graph structure matters.
method: Set absent graph edges to zero and diagonal entries to one as a matrix completion constraint.
Project an initial matrix onto the elliptope under positive semidefiniteness to obtain a valid correlation matrix.
Optionally enforce a target mean for off-diagonal entries to better mimic realistic data.
evidence_signal: The authors compare several numerical schemes through simulations and apply the method to two real-world datasets from neuroscience and finance, also contrasting it with GAN-based correlation matrix generation.
watch_item: The method is not intended to produce a uniform sample over the feasible set, so results depend on the chosen initialization and tuning of the mean constraint.
paper_title: Graph-Based Correlation Matrix Generation: A Convex Optimization Approach
